Reading docker-compose.yml

The mysql service definition: image, credentials, port, and where the data actually lives.

Figure 2.1 is this project's entire docker-compose.yml at this point in the build.

# Figure 2.1: local infrastructure (docker-compose.yml)
services:
  mysql:
    image: mysql:8.0
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD: root
      MYSQL_DATABASE: support_desk
    ports:
      - '3306:3306'
    volumes:
      - mysql-data:/var/lib/mysql

volumes:
  mysql-data:

A few parts worth naming:

  • image: mysql:8.0 — pulls the official MySQL image from Docker Hub the first time it's needed; no manual MySQL install anywhere.
  • environment — sets the root password and creates a database named support_desk automatically the first time the container starts.
  • ports: '3306:3306' — maps MySQL's default port out of the container and onto your machine, so anything running on the host (this API, a GUI client) can connect to localhost:3306 as if MySQL were installed locally.
  • volumes — without this, the container's filesystem — including your data — is thrown away every time the container stops. The named volume mysql-data persists it on disk instead, so restarting the container doesn't wipe your seeded tickets.

docker compose up -d mysql starts just this one service, in the background (-d, detached) so it keeps running without tying up your terminal.
